title: Creating Agents that Co-Create — Karina Nguyen, OpenAI
talk_summary: Karina Nguyen (OpenAI) surveys scaling paradigms (pretraining, RLHF post-training, RL on chain-of-thought) and then presents product-design vignettes from Claude-in-Slack, ChatGPT tasks, and Canvas, arguing agents will evolve from collaborators to co-innovators. It is a research/product-vision talk with almost no operational detail on running agent systems.

takeaways.technique: Async long-running tasks with human verification affordances
takeaways.what_they_do: They frame the core bottleneck of delegating long tasks (e.g. 'go off for 10 hours to research or write code') as trust, and propose solving it by giving humans fine-grained affordances to verify and edit model outputs and give realtime feedback.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the bottleneck here is trust and I believe that giving trust can be solved by giving humans new collaborative ordinances to verify edit model outputs

takeaways.technique: Critic/editor agent alongside a primary agent
takeaways.what_they_do: They describe Canvas scaling to 'multi-agents' where a model critic or editor works alongside the main model, plus multiplayer human collaboration in the same artifact.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if I can create a model critic or an editor they can use you have like a multi-agentic and multiplay collaboration at the same time

takeaways.what_they_do: ChatGPT tasks are framed as familiar scheduled reminders that become powerful because the same primitive composes with new model capabilities (daily story continuation, daily search, language learning).
takeaways.evidence_quote: your product feature should enable modular compositions that will scale very nicely in the future as the models will develop much higher capability

takeaways.what_they_do: 100K context succeeded because it was surfaced as file uploads (a familiar document metaphor) rather than an infinite chat; they argue wrapping new capability in the simplest familiar form is a design discipline.
takeaways.evidence_quote: how do you bring unfamiliar capability into familiar from factor ... finding the simplest form practice sometimes for unfamiliar capability

takeaways.technique: Stream summaries of long reasoning to the user
takeaways.what_they_do: Because reasoning models can take 15s–30min, they stream summarized model thoughts to the user so the wait is legible and the human can intervene.
takeaways.evidence_quote: have like a streaming models thoughts to a user and that way we had to communicate what exactly the summaries of the thoughts
